B1.3 Flowcharts and Pseudocode

Communicate algorithm logic with precision

Cluster A | From idea to algorithm

When is a process too vague to implement?

"Process loan requests quickly" is a goal, not an algorithm.

What detail must appear before developers can build the logic?

I do

Convert natural language into algorithm steps

Natural language: "Approve students if attendance is good and payments are complete."

INPUT attendance, feesPaid
IF attendance >= 90 AND feesPaid = TRUE THEN
    OUTPUT "Approved"
ELSE
    OUTPUT "Hold"
END IF

Now the algorithm is finite, testable, and unambiguous.

We do

Ambiguity check

Rewrite this rule so different developers produce the same output:

"If score is close to pass, allow retake."

Define exact boundary values and branch outcomes.

You do

Worksheet handoff

You Do: Complete the algorithm precision worksheet in Activities.

Translate three natural-language statements into precise algorithm form.

Cluster B | Pseudocode conventions

How do we keep pseudocode readable across languages?

Pseudocode should focus on logic, not syntax preference.

Which conventions prevent misreading?

I do

Apply standard pseudocode structure

Need Pseudocode form
Input INPUT value
Process total ← total + value
Decision IF condition THEN ... ELSE ... END IF
Output OUTPUT result

We do

Mini conversion

Take a short Python snippet and rewrite it into language-neutral pseudocode.

Check that every branch and loop remains explicit.

Cluster C | Flowchart quality

What makes a flowchart markable and reliable?

A flowchart fails when branch labels or connectors are unclear.

How do we protect decision clarity and execution flow?

I do

Build a branch-safe flowchart plan

  • Use standard symbols for process, input/output, and decision.
  • Label each decision branch explicitly (Yes/No or True/False).
  • Make every branch reconnect or terminate without dead ends.
  • Trace one test case to confirm branch logic before coding.

We do

Correct the branch logic

Given a flawed flowchart, identify:

  • One missing decision label
  • One broken connector
  • One branch that cannot reach an output

You do

Worksheet handoff

You Do: Complete the flowchart correction worksheet in Activities.

Repair branching and connector issues, then justify each correction.
